title: Stability Does Not Mirror Plasticity: A Module-Level View of Declarative and Procedural Learning in Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2611.23427v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Plasticity and stability in continual learning are typically studied at the entire-model level and in a task-agnostic manner, yet prior work has reported divergent conclusions across settings. Inspired by cognitive distinctions between declarative and procedural memory, we instead study how plasticity and stability vary across transformer modules and task types. In a controlled synthetic environment with clean measurement, we show a double dissociation: query-key (QK) and value-output (VO) projections are the most plastic on procedural tasks, whereas MLPs are the most plastic on declarative memorization. Stability, however, does not simply mirror plasticity: when learning a new procedure, updating QK retains over half of the stored declarative memory, while updating MLPs retains far less and updating VO loses roughly four-fifths. Targeted module reset-and-recovery experiments explain this asymmetry: plasticity tracks which module is best

translated_title: 稳定性并非可塑性的镜像：Transformer中陈述性与程序性学习的模块级视角
translated_abstract: 持续学习中的可塑性与稳定性通常在整体模型层面、以任务无关的方式进行研究和评估，然而已有工作在不同设置下得出了相互矛盾的结论。受认知科学中陈述性记忆与程序性记忆这一区分的启发，我们转而研究可塑性与稳定性在Transformer的不同模块和任务类型上如何变化。在一个测量干净、高度可控的合成环境中，我们展示了一种双重分离现象：查询-键（QK）投影和值-输出（VO）投影在程序性任务上最具可塑性，而多层感知机（MLP）在陈述性记忆任务上最具可塑性。然而，稳定性并非简单地镜像可塑性：在学习新程序时，更新QK投影可以保留超过一半已存储的陈述性记忆，而更新MLP所保留的要少得多，更新VO投影则会丢失大约五分之四。针对性的模块重置与恢复实验解释了这种不对称性：可塑性追踪的是哪个模块最适合……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了Transformer中可塑性与稳定性在模块层面的双重分离——QK与VO投影在程序性学习中最具可塑性而MLP在陈述性记忆中最具可塑性，并且稳定性并不镜像可塑性：学习新程序时更新QK可保留过半陈述性记忆，而更新VO会丢失约五分之四。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals a module-level double dissociation in transformers—QK and VO projections are most plastic for procedural learning while MLPs are most plastic for declarative memorization—and shows that stability does not mirror plasticity: updating QK retains over half of stored declarative memory when learning a new procedure, whereas updating VO loses roughly four-fifths.
